propositions: A 106-line CAS push loop in reconcile-bridge.yml duplicates push.py logic verbatim but has diverged in retry count (5 vs 3), final push behavior (present vs missing), and error handling, requiring consolidation into a single core entrypoint

Two YAML CAS loops across reconcile-bridge.yml and reconcile-bridge-canary.yml carry conflicting standing decisions that prevent extraction; consolidation requires explicit reversal of those decisions and replacement with thin smoke-test harnesses

push.py lacks a strict mode that fails loud on silent best-effort returns (non-retriable decline, merge-recovery failure, store-epoch guard, final-push rejection, lock timeout); strict mode must raise a catchable exception with git reason and unpushed count, translated to non-zero exit only at the private module CLI boundary

A new core entrypoint must stage+commit dirty tracker trees before pushing, preserving the reconciler's commit-back identity with explicit author name/email parameters, because moving git-add+commit into core removes it from the shell-level git config
Strict mode invoked under sync.push=off or async must raise an exception immediately rather than silently no-op, while best-effort mode retains current behavior unchanged for all existing callers

The reconciler workflow must call commit-and-push in strict mode with REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always, while the canary workflow must call push-only in strict mode, to flip disposition from red (data loss risk) to reliably red (delivery confirmed or failed loud)
